:::{#thm-linear-map-lincom}
#### A linear map preserves linear combinations

If $f: \reals^p \to \reals^m$ is a linear map (@def-linear-map),
then for any vectors $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k \in \reals^p$
and any coefficients $c_1, \ldots, c_k \in \reals$:

$$f\paren{\sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j \vecf{v}_j} = \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j f(\vecf{v}_j)$$

:::

::: proof

By induction on $k$.
For $k = 1$, the claim $f(c_1 \vecf{v}_1) = c_1 f(\vecf{v}_1)$ is homogeneity.

Suppose the claim holds for $k$ vectors. Then for $k + 1$:

$$
\ba
f\paren{\sum_{j=1}^{k+1} c_j \vecf{v}_j}
&= f\paren{\sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j \vecf{v}_j + c_{k+1} \vecf{v}_{k+1}}
&& \text{(split off the last term)}
\\&= f\paren{\sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j \vecf{v}_j} + f(c_{k+1} \vecf{v}_{k+1})
&& \text{(additivity)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j f(\vecf{v}_j) + f(c_{k+1} \vecf{v}_{k+1})
&& \text{(induction hypothesis)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j f(\vecf{v}_j) + c_{k+1} f(\vecf{v}_{k+1})
&& \text{(homogeneity)}
\\&= \sum_{j=1}^{k+1} c_j f(\vecf{v}_j)
&& \text{(join the last term back on)}
\ea
$$

:::
